cohort: The study included 150 neonates, comprising 71 preterm newborns (32-37 weeks) and 79 term newborns (>37 weeks).
finding: Preterm newborns exhibited significantly lower cord blood glucose and cortisol levels but higher insulin and HOMA-IR compared to term newborns, with insulin negatively correlating and cortisol positively correlating with gestational age.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery showed no significant differences between the preterm and term newborn groups.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken from cord blood at birth.
birth_weight: Preterm newborns averaged 2.20 +/- 0.41 kg, while term newborns averaged 2.73 +/- 0.32 kg.
gest_age: Preterm newborns were 32-37 weeks, and term newborns were >37 weeks.
